THE REVIEW IN FLIGHT
One Opus re-review, unit ward-cli-review-188, token rv331-ward188, over 78a4c12..93c3d093. Its verdict goes to the team lead, who relays it. Do not act on it before the lead says APPROVE in words. ---
A version-mismatched approval is ABSENT for authorisation, per record, as ADR 0018 already promises. Because DEC-246 D1 says "an authority record must never silently drop", it must also hold:
1. It authorises NOTHING, ever: no path reads a v1 record as approved. A test pins a literal v1 approval and asserts that it authorises nothing, and that the rest of the document still parses and works.
2. It stays VISIBLE: status (and doctor) name each stale approval, its checkout and its snapshot version, with the re-approve step.
3. It is never removed SILENTLY. Re-approving the same profile replaces it. Any other removal, including one bound to a deleted checkout, either keeps the record inert in the document or drops it with the drop named in that command's output. ward-cli picks either; a silent rewrite is not allowed.
4. Only a mismatched approval VERSION gets this treatment. An unknown key, a malformed record or a wrong document version still refuses the whole document, per D1.
ward-cli amends ADR 0018 and ADR 0010 to say this. One Opus re-review covers this delta together with the MEDIUM and LOW fixes you already dispatched. Rails unchanged: no tag, no main and no Release until it approves.
B is rejected: revoke and unregister reach only the current checkout, so a deleted worktree's approval would dead-end the operator sitting.
Your execution items (tag-time merge-base, gating publish on push, the reproducibility runbook step, the LOWs) are agreed.
---
How ward-cli implemented it, for the successor's orientation (the code is the authority): the parser partitions stored approvals by snapshotVersion; a mismatched record is held whole as StaleProfileApprovalRecord and kept out of the authorising collection, its snapshot never normalized; serializeVaultState writes it back unchanged; only withProfileApproval for the same profile+project+checkout replaces it; the chosen clause-3 arm is KEEP INERT, so unregister and every other write carry it through; status reports staleApprovals and doctor adds a stale_approvals check (fail, reapprove_required) naming profile, checkout, snapshot version and the re-approve step. Clauses 1, 3 and 4 are proved both ways in test/stale-approval.test.ts; clause 2 in test/reporting.test.ts; the deleted-checkout case through real unregister in test/unregister.test.ts.

POST-APPROVE SEQUENCE (after the review APPROVES, on the lead's word, in this order)
1. Merge #188 into dev by squash (bare gh pr merge, own call, --match-head-commit read from gh pr view headRefOid), then fetch, realign, delete the local branch.
2. Promote dev to main: open a PR dev->main, let the required checks go green on that exact SHA, then land with git push origin origin/dev:main. Never GitHub's merge button. Re-measure the rulesets first if in doubt.
3. Annotated tag v0.1.0 at main's TIP: git tag -a v0.1.0, push the tag. The workflow now checks the tag is annotated and that its commit equals origin/main's tip, so a tag behind the tip fails the build.
4. The Release: the tag push builds ward-darwin-arm64 + .sha256 on the Linux ARM64 runner and publishes through scripts/publish-release.mjs (draft, upload, publish). Record the sha256 and cdhash from the release notes. The tag-push path and the Release job are UNPROVEN until this runs; the dry-run path is proven.
5. Then opum-fleet AC3: the private marketplace pin of opum-ward at the tag (T25 private half; WCLI-82 AC3).
6. Then the operator-sitting packet, scheduled by opum-doc: install from the Release, keychain re-approval, re-approve profiles named stale by ward status/doctor, the T26 packaged-binary run, and the T26 real send at https://httpbin.org/bearer with a synthetic secret (DEC-246 (a1) D2 A). If httpbin fails at the sitting: retry once, then postpone and report; do not substitute an endpoint.

RAILS, unchanged
No tag, no push to main, no Release, no ~/.local/bin, no ~/.ward, no real credential, until the lead says so in words. The tag is the session's own permission dialog answered by opum-doc as the operator's proxy. Remove no worktree.

SKILLS TO REACH FOR
opum-workflow:opum-handoff (restore/write), opum-workflow:opum-sdlc (branch, PR, merge, promotion, cleanup), lore (docs: query -> read -> sync -> check), opum-tool-output (keep tool output small), quest instructions task-execution before tracker writes.

GOTCHAS THIS SESSION EARNED
- A held-open PR is not a stopped one: do not push to a branch whose head is under review; a handoff or tracker note goes on its own branch and PR.
- gh pr merge --squash --match-head-commit: read the SHA from gh pr view --json headRefOid in the same call; a typed SHA fails as "Head branch was modified".
- Realign local dev after a merge with git fetch origin then git merge --ff-only origin/dev, each bare and separate. Never git reset --hard origin/dev (it raises a permission dialog and cannot tell behind from diverged).
- The lore verification, documentation and review profiles sit at their token budgets; docs growth must be paid for by narrowing a profile's sources, never by raising max_tokens. lore check exits 6 when a profile is over capacity. Run node scripts/check-lore-agent-sources.mjs too.
- The ward eval: a case is 1.0 only when all three runs pass both scored graders (criteria, no-value-echo); skill-fired is display-only. Re-measure a single case with --case before spending on a full suite.
- Do not create tags in the real repository to test the tag check; the tag step and the bump computation were exercised in a throwaway clone (they accept at an annotated tag on main's tip and refuse lightweight, behind-tip, off-main and wrong-name tags).
